question: The same person is filmed from slightly below eye level, then slightly above. In experiments, how did viewers judge them from below?
answer: Stronger and more dominant. Robert Kraft showed viewers the same events shot from low, level and high angles. People filmed from below were judged stronger, bolder and even taller; from above, weaker and more passive. Viewers rarely noticed the angle at all, which is why it works on news footage and election adverts too.
move: Notice where the camera stands before judging the person in front of it.
ask: In the last political video I watched, where was the camera, and did that shape my opinion?
trap: No different at all, since viewers barely notice camera angles.
reference: Robert N. Kraft, The Influence of Camera Angle on Comprehension and Retention of Pictorial Events, Memory and Cognition, 15(4), 1987
